small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose2d itself dominates runtime here (post-processing kernels are tiny relative to the 16×128×514×514 conv-transpose). Tuning BLOCK_HW/num_warps in `fused_post_kernel` won't move the needle — the torch conv_transpose is the bottleneck.
- If keeping the structure, at minimum convert the post chain to channels_last and merge `fused_post_kernel` + `lse_kernel` into one kernel (one program per N, reduce H×W per channel into shared, then LSE across OC) to remove the workspace round-trip.
- Try `BLOCK_HW=4096` with `num_warps=16, num_stages=2` for the mean reduce, but expect <1% gain since conv-transpose is ~99% of runtime.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the input×kernel outer product and atomic-adding into the (N, OC, H+2, W+2) output. With kernel_size=3 and stride=1, each input element contributes to a 3×3 output patch — small fan-out, good for atomics or per-program accumulation.
- Better: gather-form direct kernel — one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), loop over (IC, kh, kw), gather valid input positions (i.e., `(oh-kh+pad, ow-kw+pad)` in range), accumulate into a register tile. Use channels_last input/output, BLOCK_M=64 (out spatial), BLOCK_N=64 (OC), BLOCK_K=32 (IC). Fuse the entire epilogue (mean over H×W, +bias, LSE over OC, ×10) by accumulating per-tile partial sums of the conv output and reducing across tiles via atomics into a small (N, OC) workspace, then a tiny second kernel does LSE.
- Since mean+LSE+sum collapses the entire spatial+channel dims to a scalar per N, fusion is high-value: each output pixel of the conv-transpose only needs to be accumulated into the per-channel running sum, never stored. This eliminates the (N, 128, 514, 514)≈17 GB write entirely — likely the single biggest win.
